summary: The Subir belt's third fall, between Bhalkhet and Dev Van. Undocumented until its map pin surfaced.
description:
Milan spent a year on this dataset's 'searched but not found' list: no article, no listing, no spelling of the name led anywhere. The map pin, supplied by a traveller who has stood at it, finally placed it exactly where the belt's other secrets live: the Godadiya–Subir forest country, three kilometres from Bhalkhet and five from Dev Van, making a tight triangle of falls that share the same roads, the same rains and the same near-total absence from tourism literature.

Expect the belt's standard terms: a monsoon-fed drop reached by a short walk from village roads, no facilities, no signage, and flow that lives and dies with the wet spells. Ask for 'Milan dhodh' in the surrounding hamlets, as with its neighbours, local directions beat any map.
highlights: Completes the Bhalkhet–Dev Van–Milan falls triangle
Zero web footprint, a genuinely local waterfall
Same belt roads as its better-known neighbours

modes.road: Village roads in the Godadiya–Subir belt, off the Ahwa and Waghai sides; ask locally for the Milan turn
modes.rail: Waghai (heritage narrow gauge); Bilimora Jn for broad gauge

access.last_mile: Short walk from the road end; wet-season slick
access.road_condition: Rural tar and dirt; slow in monsoon

visit.notes: Open village land; daylight visits only.

seasonality.notes: Monsoon-fed like the whole belt; thin to nothing outside the rains.

experience.photography_notes: Forest-framed falls; overcast monsoon light flatters the dark rock.

amenities.food: None. Carry everything; nearest food at Subir or Ahwa
amenities.guides: Village youths point or walk along for a tip

warnings: Wet rock is slick, grip footwear only
Flow surges after upstream rain; stay off the apron in spate

tips: String Bhalkhet, Milan and Dev Van into one Subir-belt falls run
Weekdays keep the belt to herders; reels are finding it fast
